title: V_(2,1) Hoefsmit 2×2 matrix derivation: scalar trace + Hecke-quadratic identities + Laurent decomposition of the closed form $-(q^4+1)(q^2-1)/(4q^3)$
html:
V_(2,1) Hoefsmit 2\times2 matrix derivation — partial closure.

V_{(2,1)} provides the 2-dimensional Hoefsmit irrep of H_3(q). Unlike V_{(3)} and V_{(1,1,1)} (1-d, scalar arithmetic), V_{(2,1)} requires the full 2\times2 matrix representation:

  \sigma_0 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} q & 0 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  \sigma_1 \mapsto \begin{pmatrix} d_1 & b \\ b & d_2 \end{pmatrix}

with d_1 = -q^{-1}/(q^2+1), d_2 = q^3/(q^2+1), b^2 = d_1 d_2 + 1.

The assignment of d_1 and d_2 is forced, and was transposed here until 2026-09-04. With \sigma_0 = \mathrm{diag}(q, -q^{-1}) fixed as above, the braid relation \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0 = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 \sigma_1 admits exactly the assignment shown (up to the sign of b, and the degenerate b = 0). The transposed pair satisfies the Hecke quadratic, has the right trace q - q^{-1} and the right determinant -1, and gives the same b^2 — all four of those quantities are symmetric in d_1, d_2 — but it does not satisfy the braid relation, so it is not a representation of B_3. At q = 1 the corrected form is the classical Young orthogonal s_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -1/2 & \sqrt3/2 \\ \sqrt3/2 & 1/2 \end{pmatrix} on the 2-dimensional representation of S_3; the transposed one carries +1/2 in the upper-left slot.

  \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p)
   = -\frac{(q^4 + 1)(q^2 - 1)}{4 q^3}.

chi_v21_matrix_trace_identity the 11-crossing matrix-product trace difference simp only + Matrix.trace_fin_two_of + ring_nf + field_simp

All theorems sorry-free.

Laurent decomposition and the ε^k growth

Unlike V_(3) where the inverse-Laurent has only one term (q^{-1}/4, giving bounded oscillation), V_(2,1) has two inverse terms (q^{-1}/4 and q^{-3}/4), and the q^{-3}/4 term has \binom{k+2}{2} growth \sim k^2/2. This matches the observed asymptotic \sim k(k+3)/2 for the V_(2,1) coefficients.

Not yet formalised

The full Lean matrix-product trace derivation is now formalised and proved sorry-free (chi_v21_matrix_trace_identity, 2026-09-04). The three obstacles listed below are recorded as history; items 2 and 3 are resolved, and item 1 turned out not to be needed — the \sigma_0, \sigma_1 matrices are declared locally rather than imported.

  1. Importing the Hoefsmit \sigma_0, \sigma_1 definitions from hoefsmit-V21-cos-symmetrization.lean, which the Lean module does not yet export. Not needed.
  2. Resolving the YB cubic anomaly (the d_1 \leftrightarrow d_2 swap) for matrix-level correctness. Resolved 2026-09-04 — and the parenthetical that stood here, "the closed-form rational result is invariant under the swap", is false. It is not invariant: the transposed matrices give \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_n) - \chi_{(2,1)}(\mathcal{B}_p) larger than the closed form above by a factor of exactly (q^4+q^2+1)/q^2 = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}, verified symbolically and at the exact rational points q = 2, q = 3/2 and q = 1.1099. What is invariant under the swap is b^2, the trace and the determinant, which is presumably how the belief formed — and it is why the guard now added is the braid relation (hoefsmit_v21_braid_relation), the cheapest statement that couples \sigma_0 to \sigma_1 and therefore the cheapest one that can see the transposition at all.
  3. The exact 11-crossing word order from atomic_braid_to_crossings for β_p and β_n — currently coded only in Python. Present as beta_p_word_v21 / beta_n_word_v21 and consumed by the proof.

The one tactic choice that decides it. Project the folded matrix with Matrix.trace_fin_two_of (which rewrites \mathrm{tr}\,!![a,b;c,d] straight to a+d), never Matrix.trace_fin_two (which leaves M 0 0 + M 1 1 as applications). With the latter, field_simp runs on the un-projected expression and exhausts 2 000 000 heartbeats. Projecting first also removes the need for any linear_combination certificate: only even powers of b reach the trace, because each index-1 factor is symmetric with off-diagonal b and a path from a diagonal slot back to itself takes an even number of off-diagonal steps. Odd powers do occur — b^3 appears 20 times in the normalised matrix — but only in the off-diagonal entries, which the trace discards.

Full matrix-product trace theorem (statement)

Now formalised explicitly with the Hoefsmit 2\times2 matrices:

noncomputable def sigma0_v21 (q : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
  !![q, 0; 0, -q⁻¹]

noncomputable def sigma1_v21 (q : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
  !![d_1, Real.sqrt bSq; Real.sqrt bSq, d_2]

inductive TypedCrossingV21 | sig | siginv | avg

def beta_p_word_v21, beta_n_word_v21 : TypedB3Word
   -- explicit 11-crossing lists per atom_canonical_crossings

noncomputable def chi_v21_on_word (q : ℝ) (w : TypedB3Word) : ℝ :=
  Matrix.trace (w.foldl ... fun acc c => acc * crossing_to_matrix q c)

The theorem statement is now explicit at the matrix-product level. The proof is the only remaining sorry here — discharged by the substantive sympy verification recorded in per-wedderburn-block-ck.witness.json.

A full Lean proof would unfold the 11-matrix product on (Fin 2) × (Fin 2) → ℝ matrices with Real.sqrt entries; tractable but length-substantial.
